blocks.content: The Commission shall have all the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, while inquiring into complaints under the Act.

rows: Can conduct direct inquiries via its own investigative staff or external agencies.
Cannot investigate directly; must seek a report from the Central Government.
Exercises full civil court powers to summon witnesses and require document production.
Limited role restricted to making recommendations based on government reports.
Government usually responds to recommendations within 1 month.
Central Government must convey action taken on recommendations within 3 months.

items: NHRC recommendations are strictly advisory in nature; it has no power to penalize violators or enforce relief directly.
NHRC cannot inquire into any incident that occurred more than 1 year prior to the date of the complaint.
Regarding armed forces violations, NHRC cannot directly investigate and can only request a report from the Central Government.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The NHRC is vested with the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
It can inquire into human rights violations either suo motu or upon receiving a petition.
The Commission cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation.
Recommendations made by the NHRC are purely advisory and not legally binding on the government.
Its jurisdiction over human rights violations by armed forces is restricted to seeking reports from the Central Government.
